title: Versioning Data with DVC
intro: Git versions code, but a 20GB dataset doesn't belong in git. DVC versions data alongside code: git stores small pointer files, the data itself lives in cloud storage.

steps.prompt: Initialize DVC in this git repository.
steps.fake_output:
Initialized DVC repository.
You can now commit the changes to git.
steps.explanation: Creates a .dvc/ directory with DVC's configuration, tracked by git.
steps.why: DVC layers on top of git rather than replacing it — so code and the exact data it was trained on move together in the same commit history.

steps.prompt: Configure an S3 bucket as the default remote storage for data.
steps.explanation: -d makes it the default remote for push and pull.
steps.why: Without a shared remote, data only exists on the machine that added it — the same 'trapped on a laptop' problem experiment tracking solves for metrics.

steps.prompt: Start tracking the training dataset with DVC.
steps.fake_output:
To track the changes with git, run:
	git add data/transactions.csv.dvc data/.gitignore
steps.explanation: DVC creates a small .dvc pointer file (containing the data's hash) and gitignores the real file.
steps.why: The pointer file is what goes into git. Checking out an old commit gives you the old pointer; 'dvc pull' then fetches exactly that version of the data.

steps.prompt: Upload the data to the remote.
steps.explanation: The actual data is now in S3, addressed by its content hash.
steps.why: Committing the .dvc file without running dvc push is the classic mistake — teammates get a pointer to data that doesn't exist in the remote.

steps.prompt: Check whether your local data matches what the current pointers say.
steps.explanation: The local file was changed since it was last tracked — it no longer matches the committed version.
steps.why: Training on locally-modified data that nobody versioned is how 'we can't reproduce last month's model' happens (see mlops-incident-006). dvc status before training catches it.

steps.prompt: Show the pipeline's dependency graph from data prep through training to evaluation.
steps.explanation: Stages defined in dvc.yaml, and how outputs of one feed into the next.
steps.why: 'dvc repro' uses this graph to rerun only the stages whose inputs changed — like make, but for data pipelines. Change the data and repro reruns everything downstream; change only evaluation code and it skips training.
